sourceInventory.description: Left source subfigure, labelled Cyrillic a: one rounded eye outline with a small anterior bulge on the left and posterior retinal boundary on the right. Three approximately horizontal parallel incident rays (upper, axial, lower) travel left to right. The upper and lower rays refract inward at the front, meet on the axis inside the eye before the posterior boundary, cross, and reach that boundary separated again. The axial ray passes through the same meeting. The meeting and boundary points are unlabelled; there is no source focus-dot label.
points: unlabelled upper and lower anterior ray intersections
rays: upper parallel incident and crossed refracted ray
lower parallel incident and crossed refracted ray
sourceInventory.angles: No angle label or angle arc; parallel incident directions and post-refraction inward convergence followed by crossing are instructional relationships.
sourceInventory.givens: No dimensions, coordinates or numerical angles.

sourceInventory.description: Right source subfigure, labelled Cyrillic b: the same kind of rounded eye faces left. A vertical diverging spectacle-lens symbol stands before the eye, with top arrow pointing inward/down and bottom arrow pointing inward/up. Three parallel incident rays travel left to right. Upper/lower rays spread farther from the axis between spectacles and eye, then the eye refracts them inward to the posterior axial retinal point. Two dashed backward extensions of those spread rays meet at the open axial point A left of the spectacle lens. The axial ray runs through A, lens and posterior meeting.
points: A, an open point on the axis before the spectacle lens
unlabelled farther-separated upper/lower anterior eye intersections
rays: upper parallel incident, divergent after spectacle, convergent after eye
lower parallel incident, divergent after spectacle, convergent after eye
two dashed non-propagating backward extensions to A
sourceInventory.angles: No angle label or arc; upper/lower post-spectacle slopes point away from the axis and their backward extensions meet A.
sourceInventory.givens: Only A and the subfigure label; no distances or powers.

sourceInventory.description: Top subfigure, labelled Cyrillic a: a rounded eye with a left anterior bulge receives three parallel left-to-right incident rays, upper/axial/lower. The upper/lower rays slope inward after entering the eye, but remain separated at the posterior boundary; their source-drawn solid continuations meet on the axis just beyond that boundary. A short rightward continuation remains visible. This is a would-converge construction, not actual light propagation through a living retina.

sourceInventory.description: Middle subfigure, labelled Cyrillic b: a vertical converging spectacle-lens symbol, top arrow outward/up and bottom outward/down, precedes a rounded eye. Three parallel incident rays travel left to right. Upper/lower rays bend toward the axis at the spectacle lens, become closer together before entering the eye, and after the eye meet at the posterior axial retinal point. The axial ray remains straight.

sourceInventory.description: Bottom subfigure, labelled Cyrillic v: S is an axial object point before a converging spectacle-lens symbol with outward/up and outward/down tips. S1 is an open axial point farther left than S. Three source rays leave S toward the right: an upper divergent ray, axial ray and lower divergent ray. The upper/lower rays bend at the spectacle lens and continue toward the eye less divergently, then are refracted by the eye to the posterior retinal axis. Two dashed backward extensions of the less-divergent post-spectacle rays meet S1. The source's dimension d below runs from S1's vertical drop to a vertical drop at the eye front; it is not the distance from S to the lens. The source labels S and subscripted S1 and d; it does not print 25 cm inside the figure.
